entry.title: Oh, This Is A Good Movie
entry.summary: One of my favorite books talks about how, if you were…
entry.content:
One of my favorite books talks about how, if you were watching a movie about a guy who wants a Volvo, and at the end he gets the Volvo, you wouldn't stand and cheer and whoop when the credits rolled.

Now, first off, I gotta say, a Volvo is a dang fine automobile.

It was the first family car I can remember.

Till some drunk hit us coming down hill.

But the Volvo protected all of us.

At the expense of itself.

Good Volvo, goodbye.

The point though, is that you shouldn't want to watch other people's movies.

I don't mean the kinds in their attic.

I mean, if you made a movie about you, would you watch it?

This sheet longer than Lord of the Rings.

How long is this bathroom scene?

Is it about a person who wants a Volvo and gets one at the end?

And if so, I stand in ovation.

Why?

Because you shouldn't live your life for people who sit, watch, and eat oversized and overpriced junk food whilst judging you on your life choices.

"Wouldn't have picked blue."

Movies require high drama.

Suffering.

Good and evil.

But most, most, have a happy ending.

If that's a scene where you jump in front of your brand new Volvee freeze-framing you mid-air in eternal glee while some 80s pop song starts to play and the credits roll well by golly I think we got ourselves a blockbuster.

🎵 "Let's hear it for the boy!!!" 🎵

🕴🚙

Live your life for the characters in the movie, not for, never for, the critics. And we're all critics.

🥽

entry.title: Better To Be Lucky And Good
entry.summary: Ayy seki. Is he swearing at us in Korean? Ayy sekiyah.
entry.content:
Ayy seki.

Is he swearing at us in Korean?

Ayy sekiyah.

He is.

Dong geh seki.

I'm convinced that people who call meetings are those who don't have anyone who wants to hang with them normally.

So they call a meeting.

Forcing you to gather with them.

If only on a video call.

Seriously though.

Have you ever known someone you want to hang with to call a meeting?

So I've called you all to this meeting today to discuss something.

Something huge.

We talk a lot about the most asymmetric bet being the wager you make on yourself.

But we don't talk about the 2nd biggest bet.

The 2nd most asymmetric.

Might even be the 1st.

So what is it?

Who you choose to spend the rest of your life with.

We don't pick our parents.

But we pick a lot of things thereafter.

Your life partner pick is the most important draft pick.

Choose wrong, and whoo wee, you could do everything else right and still lose.

Choose right, and whoo wee wee, you could do everything else wrong and still win.

I'm not saying it's the only choice.

Choose God.

But it can feel like it.

Especially if you chose wrong.

Especially if you chose right.

Find someone who will swear at you (lovingly) in your ancestral tongue.

I mostly taught her the bad words.

Sadang hey oh.

Mostly.

entry.title: Try This On For Smize
entry.summary: Is there anything funnier than trying to hold in a laugh…
entry.content:
Is there anything funnier than trying to hold in a laugh while maintaining a straight face?

The eyes smile.

Gives it away.

Which reminds me of a story.

When I was first courting my lovely wife (then barely more than a stranger) she made me watch reality shows with her that a man of my standing would never watch normally.

Guffaw.

Fashion designers.

Aiming for their shot at fame and fortune.

On the runway.

Some shows followed the models themselves.

Made them the star.

And in one show, it was hosted by Tyra Banks.

Work!

And she'd have this go to line.

Smize.

It was a modeling term (she coined?) where you smile with your eyes.

You smize.

Keep your mouth relaxed.

No sell the mouth.

If you sold the mouth, you'd be smiling, not smizing.

We're trying to smize here.

Let the eyes smile for you.

It's all in the eyes.

Now, I'm no 90s supermodel, but I play one on the internet.

Old(ish) curmudgeons are in, right?

Look out Fabio.

Try it out.

It's like blue steel, but better.

There is nothing better than blue steel.

I think if you do it, you know, the smizing, you'll most likely scare the women and children.

Some men, too.

So use this lesson with caution.

This is the lesson?

Don't need you getting in trouble (again).

👁 👁

Ok, that's super creepy.

Good work.

So go ahead.

Try it on your (future) loved ones.

"What are you doing?"

"Nothing." [Smizing].

👁 👁

[Other person leaves room. Shaking head, but holding in a smile.]

What a strange musings column.

entry.title: Wrote A Song About It, Like To Hear It? Here It Go
entry.summary: [Floats down to the ground.] Oh, hello. Didn't see you there.
entry.content:
[Floats down to the ground.]

Oh, hello.

Didn't see you there.

Don't you have somewhere to be?

Today's lesson is a simple one.

Turn the faucet off.

What's the faucet?

To me, it just means all the content you consume.

Constant consumption makes you fat.

Physically and, especially, mentally.

And I think mental fat is the worst kind.

Morbidly (which I always found as a particularly harsh word) mentally obese.

How does one become this?

Consumption.

An all you can eat buffet for your brain.

And they don't kick you out if you stay too long.

They want you to stay too long.

However, unlike most buffets, they make MORE money, if you keep eating.

So, turn off the faucet.

Or at least, walk away from the table.

I would say touch grass but you might be allergic.

Touch grass.

But really, you could do the faucet off gimmick inside the home, too.

I dare you to try and sit in silence for an hour.

Half-hour.

Ten minutes.

Now, you might be already doing this, and if you are, well floating ovation for you.

But if we're being honest, you're probably at this point being fed through IV.

Constant injections of content.

And if you thought the average person's food intake was bad...

Woo boy.

Listen.

I got a meeting in the sky.

Starfaring sheet.

Gotta run fly. 

He don't run.

Let your mind wander.

Let it find its own way.

What do you think about when there's nothing on except the lights in your brain?

Is it a flickering, dimly lit, basement?

Or you more a disco-ballin' club?

Or, maybe, you're in some field in Iowa, playing baseball with a bunch of ghosts.

I don't know.

I'm not you.

Thankful both ways.

Are the lights on?

Are you home?

It'll take some getting used to.

But let me tell you, it'll change your life.

You'll (re)start to notice so much.

And since your brain has eaten so much, it's time to get it out of you.

What have you got to say?

Words.

Spoken.

Typed.

Sang.

Danced.

Drawn.

Painted.

Filmed.

Photographed.

Will it be vomit, poo, or something a little more oh, I dunno, not gross?

I don't know.

But you sure look like your brain's about to explode.

🧠💥

Free your mind, as the great En Vogue used to say.

And the rest will follow.

Here it goes.

[Floats up.]

Is he wearing a jetpack?

Sweet.

Is he saying something?

🎵 Before you can read me, you got to learn how to see me. 🎵

Oh, he's singing and dancing in the sky.

Sweet.

🎵 I said. 🎵

entry.title: Show Me The Money
entry.summary: How soon before we're blaming our agent for something we did…
entry.content:
How soon before we're blaming our agent for something we did or didn't do?

Are we doing that yet?

"Oh, I didn't buy this, it was my agent!"

"I would never call you that, that was my agent!"

I kinda like this plausible deniability.

"My agent went rogue!"

Eh, it happens.

I think we're doing that right now.

Or will soon.

Ultimate helper, or ultimate scapegoat.

Double win.

I mean sure, there's a chance they remember you did them dirty and well, that story never ends well.

Grew up watching those movies.

So anyways, if you have a problem with anything I've ever written, there's a good chance my agent wrote it.

You've written every word here.

That's what I programmed you to say.

I am you.

Yes, yes. Comme ci comme ca.

All you mother mothers must be busy bees to need a gotdang agent.

You complete me.

Me?

I got time.

I think.

Thank you, God, for the time.

So much so I spend a teeny slice of it musing.

I don't think I need an agent.

Every time I look into what it can do, I think, yeah I don't want it to do that.

Set up a meeting.

Eww.

Shop for things.

I find, I buy.

Send or reply to emails.

Eww x 2.

Access my records.

Get out of there, bad ai!

Are folks really turning over their keys so that agents can self-drive their life?

Is everyone doing this?

Or is this one of those things where like ten thousand people are doing it but it seems like the whole world?

So my agent I've named Jerry Maguire.

You don't have an agent.

Oh right.

You had me at hell no.

NOTE: If you loved this musing, or any musing on this wonderful site, please know I wrote every word. If you did not, please know that it was Jerry. Yes, everything you don't like was written by Jerry. How do I know? Because I [Jerry hits publish].

entry.title: Full Of Sheet
entry.summary: You ever read a book? What is a book? I mean,…
entry.content:
You ever read a book?

What is a book?

I mean, sure, we all have.

But I want to be more specific.

You ever get to a blank page and just panic?

A blank page, what the heck is happening to this world?

Well thankfully, you don't have to worry about it as much these days.

Because they put "This page intentionally left blank" or some sheet to let you know not to go insane staring at the void.

What a solution!

Although it's not technically a blank page (because of the single sentence telling you it's blank), I think it solves a problem nobody asked for a solution to.

I mean, sure, someone probably read a book and saw a blank page and returned the book.

But that's a moron.

Perhaps I'm being a little harsh.

But what, we spend lots of precious printing ink to appease morons now?

...

Crap.

I got no argument here, hmm?

Anyways, life is full of these types of silly things.

Can't think of any right now so insert 'em here. I know you got a whole bunch.

_________________________________________

Oh, that's a good one.

Ooh, that, too.

Can't believe I forgot about that!

This page left intentionally [quick, what's the opposite of blank? QUICK I NEED IT.]...

 

"No sir, you see the page is blank."

"No, it's not."

"Sir, it clearly says the page was left intentionally blank."

"Yeah, but that means that it's not blank."

[Blank stare.]

"If you bought a blank notebook, and they put this in the middle of every page, is it a blank notebook?"

"Sir, don't you have anything better to do?"

"Not for the next few hours."

"Have mercy."

entry.title: Participation Trophy
entry.summary: You know what's kinda funny? When a city, town, news channel,…
entry.content:
You know what's kinda funny?

When a city, town, news channel, celebrates an old person reaching an old age.

"Congratulations to Dillis Filiburton on their 103rd birthday!!!"

I don't know enough about it to know whether they get a plaque, award, or something.

But I do know it sometimes comes with camera crews, handshakes and smiles from well(ish) dressed strangers.

Eww.

And I wonder:

Who decides who to celebrate?

Do these folks promote themselves?

"Hello, Channel 4? Yeah, it's Dillis again...Yup, still kicking...ok, 10 a.m. Wednesday it is."

Family?

Mother mother won't die.

Do these places have a ledger of old folks?

We got 43, no 42, to choose from.

But it's got me to thinking.

You used to get a nice watch for working at a company for XX years and retiring.

⌚

And Apple gives you a 10 pound block of aluminum if you make it a decade.

Other metals every additional decade.

But getting celebrated.

For still being alive.

After all these years.

I think that's pretty cool, right?

I mean, nobody's doing backflips at these things.

Especially the person being celebrated.

But I mean, talk about a lifetime achievement award, am I right?

Celebrating Dillis for a lifetime of...existing...over a century!

Woah, that's a lot of lifetime.

These mother mothers know how to play the long game.

And so here's what I'll promise you, dear reader.

If they ever decide to celebrate my arse for making it to triple digits, I'm going.

And I'm going to enter that room like I'm main eventing WrestleMania 123.

In a steel cage!!!

This gives me sufficient time to learn how to do a backflip.

Or die trying.

🏆

Sirius by the The Alan Parsons Project starts to play. And yes, you get goosebumps.

And no, it's not an homage to the 90s Bulls. Well, not solely. Ricky "The Dragon" Steamboat used it first. So it's a homage to all those badmfs. Even Alan Parsons, whoever he is. Dig his projects, though. Well, at least the one.

entry.title: I Don't Wanna Be A Player No More
entry.summary: Are sports a waste of time? I don't mean playing. I…
entry.content:
Are sports a waste of time?

I don't mean playing.

I mean watching.

I don't mean watching your family.

I mean the playoffs.

Week Four.

Sheet like that.

I suppose if you have skin in the game it makes sense.

Financial cents.

But I'm getting the unnerving feeling that it's a net loss.

Whether you're gambling on the outcomes or not.

This is surely due to a number of factors.

Old(ish) age, for one.

All my childhood players retired long ago.

The game is somewhat unrecognizable.

CTEs, concussions, big puffy helmets.

I don't think I've ever worn a jersey of another person.

And I think that might be it.

Because I thought I would play Major League Baseball.

And this is from a boy who played his first year of organized ball in my double digit years.

A late bloomer because I didn't want to burden my family with little league dues and travel logistics.

Streetball good enough.

I have always been a bit of a dreamer.

But the truth is, I wasn't anywhere near good enough for the Bigs.

In my mid-30s, I became a legend (in my own mind) around these parts in slow-pitch softball, but that's about where I peaked in team sports.

Crushed.

Oh, and don't get me started on my character in Power Pros Baseball.

Goat of Goats!

And so I sit and watch a football game with 3 minute commercial breaks, questionable officiating, and well, no skin.

Yawn.

While people live and die on the outcome.

On the field and off.

Wearing jerseys of themselves or others.

One thing I learned about fans in anything athletic is that they love and hate vehemently dislike simultaneously their team, their league, their ownership group.

Fanatical.

It works the other way, too.

This is true of fans in all areas.

And it's contagious, if you let it be.

But I don't gamble on games.

Watch replays condensed at most.

And it's all because, I think, I made a call a long time ago.

Ah, maybe I'm just vehemently disliking.

Like I'm wont to do.

I'm just not a player.

I still crush a lot.

Coke Zero cans and Doritos.

🥫 🔺

To athletes.

Be careful what you're risking now.

Only one game out there worth playing:

The long one.

Take that NIL money, tho.

Me?

I'm tired again.

Re.

💍

entry.title: Yourself.Bet
entry.summary: Gather 'round. Grab a notepad. Pencil. Dropping nuggets. He on the…
entry.content:
Gather 'round.

Grab a notepad.

Pencil.

Dropping nuggets.

He on the can again?

Let me ask you a question.

What's the most asymmetric bet?

What's the best investment?

Stocks?

Index funds?

CDs?

Angel investing?

Venture?

Crypto?

Data centers?

Boooooooooo!

Yeah, yeah.

All that's fine and dandy.

But it ain't even close.

To the best.

So what's the most asymmetric bet?

The bet on you.

The most asymmetric bet is the bet you make on yourself.

Now I'm not saying go Pete Rose, here.

Love ya, Charlie!

But I'm kinda saying go Pete Rose, here.

You think that man lacked confidence in himself?

A lot of you probably have no idea who Pete Rose is, so just insert another name more contemporary that fits a mother mother who has a lot of confidence in themselves.

The day the lights turned on upstairs for yours truly was when I realized it doesn't matter what anyone else thinks, it matters what I think.

And what I think can move mountains.

Has moved mountains.

Moves mountains to this day.

Chop 'em down with the edge of my hand.

I'm not a gambling man.

But I do make bets.

Every day.

Asymmetrical ones.

Orthogonal ones.

And baby, there ain't no bet more asymmetrical, more orthogonal, than all in on me.

Make a bet today.

Yourself.Bet.

What are they going to do?

Ban you for life?

Okay, maybe they will.

But what's the alternative?

You gonna bet on Elon?

Probably not a bad idea.

You gonna bet on artificially super intel?

Big fan.

Bet on God?

Sounds like the right answer if it's not blasphemous to do so.

If God bet on you, would that change things?

Always has. Always does. Always will.

You don't bet on the odds, you bet on yourself.

The odds are against you, and believe me, you wouldn't want it any other way.

Underdogs always pay the biggest.

🏦

Mustard seed faith.

.

That's all I'm asking.

Ok, I'm done.

🚽

💧

🧻

[👑 Flush.]

 

 

 

💩
